page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-32-lssd is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of system memory. Operating on the arm64 architecture, this instance establishes an 8 GB RAM per vCPU ratio without hardware hyperthreading or x86-specific instruction set extensions. The instance profile does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

Storage architecture features 2416 GB of integrated local NVMe solid-state storage distributed across six drives. This high-density local NVMe array provides low-latency block access directly on the host, avoiding network encapsulation overhead for high-throughput input and output operations. Local solid-state drives are ephemeral and require external replication or snapshotting architectures for persistent state management. The instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual private cloud configuration or external IP reservation for public network egress.

From a cost-efficiency and hardware perspective, the c4a-highmem-32-lssd delivers high resource density by pairing power-efficient Arm cores with an expansive memory footprint and bundled local scratch storage. Bundled local NVMe capacity eliminates the requirement to provision large network-attached block volumes for temporary disk tiers. Workloads suited for this server include in-memory databases, distributed caching platforms, real-time analytics engines, and intensive ETL pipelines requiring substantial memory alongside fast local scratch space.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-32-lssd is a memory-dense virtual machine powered by 32 dedicated vCPUs on the arm64 architecture. The server provides 256 GB of system RAM, establishing a generous 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 2416 GB of local NVMe SSD storage partitioned across six drives. It operates without GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The local NVMe disk array supplies low-latency, high-IOPS temporary storage directly connected to the host, complementing the substantial memory footprint while eliminating network block storage latency. With dedicated Arm compute cores and a dense allocation of memory and fast disk, the configuration yields balanced resource efficiency for memory-intensive and I/O-sensitive operations. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, distributed key-value stores, real-time stream processing, and heavy ETL batch pipelines requiring rapid local scratch space.
